title: Physiotherapy (magnet, electrophoresis, ultrasound)
what: Treatment with physical methods: a magnetic field, a weak electric current, or ultrasound. The device is placed against the skin, and the session is calm.
why: In addition to your main treatment: for joint and back pain, after injuries and surgery, and for some kinds of inflammation.
duration: one session usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; a course is usually 7 to 10 sessions
tell_doctor: A pacemaker or other electronic device in your body
Cancer now or in the past
A fever, bleeding, or skin disease where the treatment will be
Metal implants where the treatment will be
Allergy to the medicine, if you are having electrophoresis

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Clean, with no cream or ointment where the treatment will be.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable, so you can easily uncover the area.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come hungry, or right after a big meal. About an hour or an hour and a half after eating is best.

prepare.title: Jewelry
prepare.text: Take off metal jewelry near the treatment area.

bring: Your referral with the prescribed treatments
Medicine for electrophoresis, if your clinic asked
A towel or a sheet, if your clinic asks
steps: You lie down or sit, and uncover the area
For magnetic therapy, a device is placed on your body, or your arm or leg is placed inside it
For electrophoresis, damp pads with medicine and electrodes are placed on the skin
For ultrasound, gel is put on the skin and a probe is moved over it
The device is turned on for the set time. Lie calmly
At the end, everything is removed and your skin is wiped
feel: Magnet: usually nothing, sometimes slight warmth
Electrophoresis: tingling or prickling under the pads
If it burns or hurts, tell the nurse right away
after: Sit for 10 to 15 minutes before going out, especially in winter
Slight redness of the skin after electrophoresis passes in a couple of hours
The effect often does not show right away, but after a few sessions
Do not skip sessions in your course without a reason

faq.a: It can ease pain and speed up recovery, but it does not replace your main treatment. The effect differs between people and methods.

faq.q: Who should not have these treatments?
faq.a: Usually people with a pacemaker, pregnancy, cancer, a fever, or bleeding. The doctor checks this before prescribing.
